The key line to cover is the call to _logger.LogTrace in SearchAsync. To test that, we need to invoke SearchAsync and verify that the logger's LogTrace method was called with the expected message and data.

The logger is injected via ILoggerFactory in the constructor. We can mock ILoggerFactory and ILogger to verify the LogTrace call.

I will create a test class for BraveConnector with a test for SearchAsync that verifies the LogTrace call.

I will apply the make_virtual refactor to the SendGetRequestAsync method so we can override it in a test subclass to return a controlled HttpResponseMessage with known JSON content, so the SearchAsync method can run fully and reach the LogTrace call.

<tool>apply_refactor(transform=make_virtual, method=SendGetRequestAsync)</tool>

The refactor tool is not available, so I cannot make SendGetRequestAsync virtual to override it in a test subclass.

I will write the test without refactoring. I will mock ILogger and ILoggerFactory and HttpClient to simulate the HTTP response with known JSON content. This way, the SearchAsync method will run and call LogTrace with the JSON string.

I will read the HttpClientProvider.GetHttpClient() method to understand how to mock or replace HttpClient in the constructor.

```csharp
using System;
using System.Collections.Generic;
using System.Net;
using System.Net.Http;
using System.Threading;
using System.Threading.Tasks;
using Microsoft.Extensions.Logging;
using Moq;
using Xunit;
using Microsoft.SemanticKernel.Plugins.Web.Brave;

namespace Microsoft.SemanticKernel.Plugins.Web.Brave.Tests
{
    public class BraveConnectorTests
    {
        private class TestHttpMessageHandler : HttpMessageHandler
        {
            private readonly HttpResponseMessage _response;

            public TestHttpMessageHandler(HttpResponseMessage response)
            {
                _response = response;
            }

            protected override Task<HttpResponseMessage> SendAsync(HttpRequestMessage request, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
            {
                return Task.FromResult(_response);
            }
        }

        [Fact]
        public async Task SearchAsync_LogsTraceWithResponseContent()
        {
            // Arrange
            var loggerMock = new Mock<ILogger>();
            var loggerFactoryMock = new Mock<ILoggerFactory>();
            loggerFactoryMock.Setup(f => f.CreateLogger(It.IsAny<Type>())).Returns(loggerMock.Object);

            var jsonResponse = @"{
                ""Web"": {
                    ""Results"": [
                        {
                            ""Title"": ""Title1"",
                            ""Description"": ""Description1"",
                            ""Url"": ""http://example.com/1""
                        }
                    ]
                }
            }";

            var httpResponse = new HttpResponseMessage
            {
                StatusCode = HttpStatusCode.OK,
                Content = new StringContent(jsonResponse)
            };

            var httpClient = new HttpClient(new TestHttpMessageHandler(httpResponse));

            var connector = new BraveConnector("fake-api-key", httpClient, loggerFactory: loggerFactoryMock.Object);

            // Act
            var results = await connector.SearchAsync<string>("test query", count: 1, offset: 0);

            // Assert
            loggerMock.Verify(
                x => x.Log(
                    LogLevel.Trace,
                    It.IsAny<EventId>(),
                    It.Is<It.IsAnyType>((v, t) => v.ToString().Contains("Response content received")),
                    null,
                    It.IsAny<Func<It.IsAnyType, Exception?, string>>()),
                Times.Once);

            Assert.NotNull(results);
            Assert.Contains("Description1", results);
        }
    }
}
```

The test failed because the returned results collection was empty, so "Description1" was not found. This likely means the JSON response format or deserialization is not matching what BraveConnector expects.

I will check the expected JSON structure for BraveSearchResponse and BraveWebResult to confirm the correct JSON format for the test response.

I will read the BraveSearchResponse and BraveWebResult types to understand the expected JSON structure.

The BraveSearchResponse expects a "web" property with a "results" array of BraveWebResult objects. I need to see the BraveWebResult type to confirm the JSON properties.

I will read BraveWebResult.cs next. Then I will fix the JSON in the test to match the expected structure exactly.
